title: Make Yourself More Interesting in the New Year
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This New Year's entry distinguishes between showing interest in others and being interesting to them, arguing the two are often conflated. Showing interest is about attentiveness given to someone else, while being interesting is about what that person offers in return — and the piece argues the durable version of 'interesting' comes not from exotic experiences but from how a person thinks. Leaders who hold genuinely unique, well-reasoned viewpoints on topics that matter become magnetic over time, more so than those who simply have colorful résumés. The piece closes with a challenge to intentionally cultivate distinctive perspectives as a New Year's resolution.
points: Showing interest in others and being interesting to others are different and often confused.
Novel experiences make someone interesting only in the short term.
What sustains long-term interest is how a person thinks, especially holding unique, well-reasoned viewpoints.
Cultivating a distinctive stance on important topics is described as a matter of intention, not luck.
quotes: People move toward those they find more interesting, and they present those folks with opportunities often denied to others whom they find more commonplace.
Interest in others is about what you give, no matter how exciting they seem.
But what makes people interesting over the long term is not what they do or have done, but in how they think.
We are most drawn to people who think differently than others.
Generating unique views is not as hard as many believe, although it does take time, deep reflection, and a creative openness to see things others don’t.
How interesting are you? Make it a point to become more interesting this year.
